name: Moss and the Midnight Garden
description: A little mouse waits up late to see the one flower that only blooms at midnight.

chapters.title: The Promise of a Bud
text: At the bottom of the old stone wall there was a garden, and in the garden there was a single silver bud. Moss, a small gray mouse, had watched it for nine days. His grandmother had told him the secret: this flower opens only at midnight, and only once.
Tonight was the night. Moss packed a thimble of warm milk, a button-sized pillow and a very large amount of patience. Then he sat down beside the bud and waited.

chapters.title: Waiting
text: Waiting, Moss discovered, is a kind of listening. He heard the crickets begin their evening song. He heard a leaf let go of a branch and take a very long time to land. He heard his own breathing slow down, until it matched the breathing of the garden.
A snail came by and shared a story about a very tall tomato. A moth landed on the pillow and fell asleep at once. The moon rose over the wall and the shadows grew long and kind.
Moss blinked. Once. Twice. The bud did not move. "Not yet," whispered the garden, and Moss nodded, because he was not in any hurry at all.

chapters.title: Midnight
text: Somewhere far away a clock took a deep breath and began to chime. One. Two. Three. And as the twelfth chime floated over the wall, the silver bud shivered and unfolded, one petal after another, like a hand opening in its sleep.
The whole garden lit up with a soft pearly glow. Every leaf looked as if it had been dipped in moonlight. The scent was the smell of every good evening Moss had ever had.

He did not say a word. He only sat and looked, with his chin in his paws, until his eyes grew heavy. In the morning he woke up curled on his pillow, with a single silver petal tucked under his arm, and he knew that it had not been a dream.
